_schema.name: output basename; renders to art/sprites/<name>.png
_schema.fit: 'footprint' scales XY to fill the footprint; 'height' scales Z to height_tiles
_schema.height_tiles: required when fit=height. Tall thin assets MUST use height - a pole's footprint carries no usable scale signal
_schema.yaw_correction: degrees to rotate so the front faces -Y. Determined from an 8-way turnaround, never guessed
_schema.states: map of state name -> hook filename in art/blender/states/, or null
_schema.yaws: [0,90,180,270] for 4-way buildings; [] for fixed. Cell is unioned across all four
_schema.hsv: optional {hue,saturation,value} correction injected before Base Color
_schema.status: real | reference | proxy | test | calibration. 'calibration' is the permanent synthetic HF floor - untextured flat-shaded geometry, committed and never regenerated. A real asset must never be the floor: a floor cannot include the thing it measures.
_schema.glow_at: furnace/firebox position in tiles, after yaw_correction. Drives the emitter fallback until the magenta mask is validated on a real generation.
_schema._mask: Any region that should glow is painted flat #FF00FF in the CONCEPT IMAGE. normalize.neutralize_mask() replaces it with a dark cavity colour in every state; the smelting hook lights that same mask. Validate per asset with art/tools/keymask.py.
_schema.albedo_gain: per-channel gain measured by art/tools/palette_drift.py (palette -> observed). Normalization applies its INVERSE so every asset lands on a common reference. Tripo's shift is not consistent between generations, so this cannot be fixed by prompting.
_schema.albedo_correction: 'remap' (per-cluster), 'gain' (single per-channel), or 'none'. Measured per asset; Tripo's shift is not consistent between generations so it cannot be fixed by prompting.
_schema.albedo_remap: per-cluster anchors from palette_drift.py --emit. Each trusted cluster carries its own gain; a texel gets the gaussian-weighted blend. Anchors are dropped when the match is not close AND decisive (d1 < min-pair and d1/d2 < 0.8). Gains are bounded by a SAFETY RAIL at 12x that should never bind - if it does, the match is wrong and it says so loudly.
_schema.palette_era: must equal lock.PALETTE_ERA. Build FAILS on mismatch - an asset generated against a superseded palette cannot enter the consistency verdict, and the albedo remap cannot retarget it (that recolours rather than corrects). Proxies are exempt.
_schema.palette_members: which locked-palette members this asset actually uses. Matching is restricted to these; an undeclared member is SKIPPED, not attempted and dropped. Attempting a colour the building was never going to contain is a category error - and the greedy assignment wastes a cluster on it.
_schema.albedo_pinned: true = approved pixels are frozen: --emit refuses to overwrite and the render says so. Pin means 'requires explicit re-approval', never 'frozen forever' - a pipeline improvement applies to every asset and every affected approval gets re-reviewed.

assets.name: _calib_floor
assets.note: PERMANENT HF FLOOR. Untextured flat-shaded battered block, generated once by art/blender/make_calibration.py and committed. NEVER regenerate it - regenerating moves the floor, which is exactly the failure it exists to prevent. Whatever HF the downsample destroys here is the irreducible cost of geometry, silhouette and rig at this camera; everything above it is what an asset's TEXTURE costs.

assets.name: smelter
assets.note: REFERENCE ASSET - APPROVED AND PINNED at 1x on the eye sheet, after the clamp raise to 12x and the re-emit. Tripo SMELTER.glb: squared block, large courses, no overhang either side, magenta firebox mask, all four declared palette members matching with zero drops. Because it has zero drops, the nearest-texel rescue cannot fire on it - verified bit-identical after that change. Prompted with the superseded draft palette, which is how we established the prompt palette is ADVISORY - see PIPELINE.md section 14.

assets.name: power_pole
assets.note: APPROVED AND PINNED (v5, one-sided design). Tall-thin case: fit=height is mandatory, the 1x1 footprint carries no usable scale signal. Cell 1x3. yaw_correction 0 confirmed by turnaround - the equipment falls on the key-lit left, and at yaw 90/270 it vanishes (0.6% silhouette asymmetry), so facing is load-bearing on this asset in a way it is not on the smelter. First asset to use the nearest-texel rescue: verdigris is 4.31% of the texture and never won a centroid at K=18. WEAKEST OF THE APPROVED SET, and the reason is EQUIPMENT REACH - not colour, not silhouette. The cross read is gone (asymmetry 52%, mast-above 18%) and the palette lands. What is weak is that the transformer box widens the outline from 13px to 19px and stops, so at 1x it reads as a post with a small cluster near the top. When Pole Tiers needs variants, start there: project the box further from the mast. Its value contrast is already 2.08x against the oak and does not need changing.
